parityComparison.ariaLabel: Reveal Steel terrain over vanilla terrain
parityComparison.captionStrong: Steel and vanilla at the same seed and coordinates.
parityComparison.captionBody: Drag the handle to compare the generated worlds. Cross-chunk features such as trees can differ in this live comparison because their final placement depends on neighboring chunk-generation order; the parity tests use a fixed order so their results are reproducible.

tickArchitecture.title: Continuous work, one safe boundary
tickArchitecture.figcaption: Conceptual timing, expanded for clarity rather than measured to scale. Chunk sending validates the player send epoch, holder identity, ticking-readiness generation, and packet-content revision before committing a packet.

healthy.label: Normal cadence
healthy.title: Packets keep flowing while background work overlaps
healthy.description: Packet workers use the whole inter-tick window instead of building one large queue for the next game tick. At the boundary, admission closes briefly while ready scheduler state and gameplay are applied safely.

slow.label: Slow scheduler
slow.title: The game tick skips the handoff instead of waiting
slow.description: Epoch A is still running at +50 ms, so the game tick keeps the last committed chunk state and continues. Once the epoch becomes Ready, a later boundary commits it and launches Epoch B.

changed.label: Chunk changed
changed.title: A revision check prevents stale chunk data from escaping
changed.description: The sender snapshots revision 42, but gameplay changes the chunk to revision 43 while it is being encoded. The old result fails validation, is discarded, and the next pass starts from fresh state.
